title: Losing a job
hook: honest work lost, and the sangat helping
tomorrow: uncle's last paycheck came up short. speak up, or let it go?

segments.voice: A hard week, and its lines. Be good company, a smell, not a speech. Pray and heal, Ardas and the form. Care for the carers, a thermos and a night shift. Ask for help, the way Ardas asks. And yesterday, get up: everyone errs, only the Guru never does. One more hard thing.
screen: `A HARD WEEK, AND ITS LINES.` → `GET UP.` → `ONE MORE HARD THING.`

segments.voice: Gurpreet uncle has driven for the same warehouse since before Simran was born. On Monday the doors have a printed sign taped to the glass: closed, effective today. He comes over that night and sits at the kitchen table with his keys still in his hand, like he might need them. He doesn't say much. He keeps saying, I always worked. Simran pours him tea and doesn't know what to do with her hands.
screen: `A SIGN TAPED TO THE GLASS.` → `KEYS STILL IN HIS HAND.` → `I ALWAYS WORKED.`

segments.voice: In Sikhi, honest work is close to the center. Kirat karni, earning by your own effort, sits beside remembering the Name and sharing what you have. On Ang 1245, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: one who eats what he earns by his labor, and gives some of it from his own hands, Nanak, that one knows the way. Gurpreet uncle has lived both halves of that line, the earning and the giving. Losing the job doesn't erase the kirat; the warehouse closed, not his worth. And now the giving comes back around, because a sangat is a lot of hands. Harjit can't hire him right now, so he calls three other trucking companies before breakfast. Bebe, still on a walker, sends a container of dal home with him. Simran sits with him at the laptop and fixes the résumé he hasn't touched in years. Nobody fixes it in a week. But he isn't carrying the sign alone.
screen: `KIRAT KARNI: HONEST WORK.` · `ANG 1245: EARN, AND GIVE.` · `THE JOB ENDED, NOT HIS WORTH.` · `CALLS, DAL, A RESUME.` · then, large: `NOT ALONE.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands open on your knees and look at them for the whole sit: the palms, the knuckles, whatever work they've done. If you pray, you can thank the Giver for the work they've had and ask for work for someone who's searching; if not, just look, and let the hands be honored.
Losing a job. Honest work ended, worth intact, and the sangat's hands reaching in.
Hold onto this: not alone, because the hands that gave are met by hands. Two weeks of living it, done.

screen: `DAY 1722 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 96 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: THE LAST PAYCHECK CAME UP SHORT. SPEAK UP?`

howItsDone: When someone loses work, Sikh families and sangats pass on job leads, help with applications, share meals, and sometimes help from daswandh, the tenth given for others.
